and development plans were not specific in terms of the number of units and layout, amongst other things. Given that redevelopment could occur in unanticipated locations without a public forum, due to the blob nature of these approved development plans, the Board amended the zoning ordinance to change the process from an administrative approval to a legislative process with public hearings for PRC plans.

When a PRC plan process was changed, there was no update to the provisions related to when a PRC plan was exempt. The current provisions largely mirror those that have been in place since 1994. Essentially, what staff will be proposing is that PRC districts use the same process as other districts when minor changes are being requested administratively.

The Zoning Ordinance requires that all uses have a PRC plan, with some exceptions. Staff reviewed these exceptions and started to compare how they relate to minor modification provisions in the Zoning Ordinance, which is how non-PRC districts are permitted to make administrative approvals for modifications.

In a PRC district, a site may be exempt based upon the provisions on this slide or if they meet the minor modification provisions. When staff begin to review and compare the PRC plan exceptions and minor modifications, we determine that they're very similar and reach a conclusion that instead of expanding the PRC plan exceptions, instead we should consolidate many of these provisions with minor modifications.

Minor modifications are administrative approvals that are reviewed by a zoning evaluation division in accordance with provisions of the zoning ordinance. These applications are coordinated with the district supervisor and require formal submission to staff.

PRC permits building additions of the lesser of 10% or 2,000 square feet, whereas a minor modification permits a building addition of the greater of 500 square feet or 5% up to 2,500 square feet, or an addition equal to 1% of a building for developments over 250,000 square feet.

Minor modifications require a notice when a building addition is proposed to adjacent property owners, but it is not the same requirement for the PRC plan exceptions. Staff recommends removing the PRC plan exceptions related to additions, since most of these additions can still be approved using the minor modification provisions.

This will permit the same building addition as every other zoning district is allowed. On here you'll see an example of where a PRC plan would permit versus the minor modification provisions for different building sizes. Buildings under 5,000 square feet or over 40,000 square feet get bigger additions using the minor modification provisions, Whereas between 5,000 and 40,000 square feet, a PRC district could get a bigger addition than any other zoning district.

Staff proposes remove this discrepancy and use the minor modification provisions only. PRC plans are not required to increase parking areas or changes to transistor screening as long as the change does not exceed 10% of the element.

Whereas minor modifications can also approve changes to transistor screening and other site elements. Both require a review of the impact on adjacent property owners. In staff opinion, these non-structural site elements can be adequately reviewed using the minor modification provisions and the separate PRC plan exceptions could be removed.

PRC plans permit minor accessory structures to open space, and a corresponding minor modification would also permit minor accessory structures and changes to open space. Again, in staff's opinion, eliminating the PRC plan exceptions language would still permit these additions under the modern modification provisions.

Finally staff is proposing a new change to minor modification which would be countywide impact and this would allow for Changes of active recreation with other active recreations of similar type size and impact this is consistent with current Consistent with past approvals for minor modifications again as I mentioned We have a dedicated web page that provides information on this topic as well as some upcoming community meetings We would have it over the next month And we'd be happy to answer any questions.
